gtlmodular.lazy_pattern_assembly.tooltip: §7§bLazy slots§7: steady-state capacity = §6highest used slot + 1 + 2 reserved§7, so an empty machine builds only 2 slots instead of all 160/640.
§7§bOne-shot batch growth§7: writing N patterns at once first expands the capacity to "used + N + reserved", so §6you never have to insert them over several rounds§7.
§7The pattern storage keeps the old §fpatternInventory§7 key, and legacy full-length internalInventory tags are still readable (aligned by index; unreadable slots are treated as empty).

§aImplemented§7: lazy slot building + one-shot batch growth, paginated pattern grid, per-slot recipe mode (auto-detect / manual assign / conflict warning), automatic mode rotation, name following, per-slot catalyst slots, pattern scale / div-scale / FOA (view rewriting), pattern identity gate (checks the recipe belongs to that slot's pattern before consuming inputs). §7Still to come§8: proxy mirroring, wireless ME, embedded circuit.
gtlmodular.super_pattern_assembly.toolti: §7Integrated §6AE2 pattern provider§7: place it in a multiblock and it reads the controller's §frecipe types§7 automatically; ME-style id, joins a §bwireless ME network§7.
§7Pattern slots: §6640§7 (max 4 pages x 160); its casing texture matches GTL Add's §bSuper Pattern Buffer§7.
§7§bPer-slot recipe mode§7: a pattern's mode is detected from its §boutputs§7; you can also assign it manually (slot number on the mode page, or §bShift + right/middle-click§7 a slot).
§7§bAutomatic mode rotation§7: when the current mode runs dry, it switches to another mode that has materials waiting, so one machine can run several modes in turn.

§7§bNo recipe mixing§7: mode lock on push + type gate / §bpattern identity gate§7 on consumption (turns gtlcore's inventory-driven matching into slot-identity-driven). Both toggleable in the mod config screen.
§7§bPattern scale§7: scales only what AE sees - stored pattern items are never touched; the ratio can apply to inputs or outputs.
§7§bFOA pattern mode§7: multiplies both inputs and outputs (1~30, default 15) without touching the original patterns.
§7§bDedicated catalyst slots§7: middle/right-click a pattern slot to open them; a §bvirtual ingredient§7 there makes that input non-consumed.
§7§bData stick mirroring§7: right-click this machine with a data stick to store its position, then right-click the pattern buffer proxy/mirror to link them.
gtlmodular.pattern_assembly.catalyst.tip: Middle-click a pattern slot to open its catalyst slots; if another mod steals the middle click, pick a slot number here and press Open
gtlmodular.pattern_assembly.archive.copy: §7Stores this machine's whole buffer (patterns + per-slot recipe type + manual assignment + per-slot catalysts and cache threshold) into the §bPattern Buffer Archive§7 item in your hand; §athis machine is not touched at all§7. §cEvery pattern taken consumes 1 blank pattern (ae2:blank_pattern) from your inventory§7; if you have too few, the whole copy is §crejected§7 (machine, tool and inventory all untouched). §8An archive made by copy can be pasted repeatedly.
§7Same copy, but §cthe source machine is emptied only after the copy succeeded§7 (write first, clear later). Clearing then invalidates the caches and makes AE re-read the pattern table through the existing path. §eCutting costs no blank patterns, but the archive can be pasted only once§7 - the tool is cleared right after a successful paste.
gtlmodular.pattern_assembly.archive.past: §7Writes the tool's archive into this machine; the placement is chosen by the Placement button on this page: §bdefault = append§7 (starts at the slot right after this machine's highest used slot and extends onwards, §anever overwrites an existing pattern§7); toggled on = §eslot-index aligned§7 (uses the archive's slot indices and §askips§7 slots that are already occupied, never overwriting them). If the capacity cannot hold it, the whole paste is §crejected§7 (not a single slot is written and the capacity is not grown either).
gtlmodular.pattern_assembly.archive.clea: §7Clears only the archive data inside the tool (the tool itself stays in your hand).
gtlmodular.pattern_assembly.archive.incl: §7When enabled, the archive also carries §bscale / divisor / forge-of-the-antichrist / output mode§7, and pasting only writes them when this is enabled on the target too. §8Off by default - settings belong to the machine, not to the patterns.
§7When enabled, the archive also carries the §bmachine name§7, and pasting only overwrites the target's name when this is enabled there too. §8Off by default.
gtlmodular.pattern_assembly.archive.hint: §8Right-click machine: empty=copy / has archive=paste / sneak=cut; sneak-right-click air=clear
gtlmodular.pattern_assembly.archive.item: §7Right-click a pattern buffer: empty tool = copy everything, with content = paste; sneak-right-click = cut. The Archive page in the machine UI has the full set of buttons.
gtlmodular.pattern_assembly.archive.held: §7The tool already holds §6%s§7 patterns: right-click a pattern buffer to paste, sneak-right-click air to clear.
gtlmodular.pattern_assembly.archive.resu: §aCopied §6%s§7 patterns (with per-slot recipe types / manual assignments / catalysts and thresholds) into the tool; §cconsumed §6%s§7 blank patterns§7.
§cNot enough blank patterns - rejected as a whole: this copy needs §6%s§7 blank patterns while you carry only §6%s§7 - §athe source machine, the tool and your inventory are all untouched§7.

§aCut §6%s§7 patterns: the archive is in the tool, the source machine is emptied and AE will re-read the pattern table. §eA cut archive can be pasted only once (the tool is cleared right after a successful paste).
§eThe cut archive was consumed by this paste (§6%s§7 patterns); the tool is now empty - §7cut or copy again to move patterns somewhere else.

§aPaste done (append mode): placed right after this machine's highest used slot - §6%s§7 patterns written, §6%s§7 metadata entries, §6%s§7 failures, §6%s§7 occupied slots skipped; this machine's capacity is at least §6%s§7 slots (a paste that does not fit is rejected as a whole, never left half-done).
§cThe source machine's pattern buffer is empty - nothing to archive.
§cThe tool holds no archive: copy or cut a pattern buffer first.

§cCannot fit - rejected as a whole: this paste needs §6%s§7 pattern slots (including reserved free slots) while this machine's hard limit is §6%s§7 - §anothing here was touched and the capacity stays exactly as it was (the capacity is fixed and never grows automatically)§7. Use a pattern buffer with more slots, or archive fewer patterns (append mode starts after the highest used slot).
§cFailed to write into the tool (tool unchanged, source machine untouched).
§cThis archive contains nothing that could be written (skipped).
§cThis machine is not handled by this archive tool: it does not hold patterns itself. Real pattern buffers - ours, gtlcore's and gtladditions' - can all be right-clicked directly.
§cThis step only works on the server (the client never writes data).
§cArchive operation failed and was aborted (data stays as before the operation; see the log).

§aPaste done (slot-index aligned): §6%s§7 patterns written, §6%s§7 metadata entries, §6%s§7 failures, §e§6%s§7 occupied slots skipped§7 (never overwritten); this machine's capacity is at least §6%s§7 slots (a paste that does not fit is rejected as a whole, never left half-done).
§cIn aligned mode all §6%s§7 target slots are already occupied - not a single slot was written (never overwrites). Turn off "Placement: slot-index aligned" to append instead.
§cPaste had no effect: all §6%s§7 slot writes failed (the machine stays as before the operation; see the log).
gtlmodular.pattern_assembly.archive.plac: §7How a paste is placed: §bdefault = append§7 - starts at the slot right after this machine's highest used slot and extends onwards, §anever overwriting an existing pattern§7 (on an empty machine this starts at slot 1, identical to aligned mode). §eToggled on = slot-index aligned§7: uses the archive's slot indices (for cloning/migrating onto another machine with the same layout); §cslots that already hold a pattern are skipped, never overwritten§7, and the number skipped is reported in the result message.

§7Values are taken from the code, not from docs:

§7* Tier 2 => §bthat family duration x0.8§7 (special-curve families ramp x0.8/x0.6/x0.5)

gtlmodular.nanochip.calibration.denomina: Denominator: recorded count, while the window is not full

The calibration denominator is the divisor of each family share.
§7"Fixed 100000"§7: the divisor is always the whole history window 100000, so tier 1 20％ needs 20,000 matching circuits.
§7"Recorded count"§7: the divisor is what the window currently holds, so tiers come far sooner while the window is filling; identical once 100,000 circuits are recorded.
§7Only the divisor changes: window size, batch count, the 8 bar families ("specials" is merged into supracausal) and both threshold sets (normal four 0.2/0.4/0.6, special-curve three 0.01/0.05/0.20) are unchanged.
§7Switch it in §fconfig/gtlmodular-common.toml§7 -> §fnanochipComplex.calibrationUseFullWindow§7, true = fixed 100000; it is also switchable in the §fin-game mod config screen -> NAC 校准与排障§7, applied as soon as you save - no restart needed.

gtlmodular.cc.tooltip.cc.howto:
§7With §asimple logistics mode§7 enabled, the host searches assembly and conversion recipes together; buffers need not switch its mode.
§7AE: connect a §bnative gtlcore ME pattern buffer§7 in the host §fH slots§7 to ME, encode separate processing patterns from JEI for real item → CC and CC → real item, then order at the ME terminal. Mirrors are optional.
§7Ordinary input buses in §fH slots§7 can also supply items; provide matching outputs to collect products. AE return requires an output-capable device connected to ME. A matching conversion recipe is required; §cprocessed PC cannot be reverted§7.
gtlmodular.cc.tooltip.pc.howto: §7A processed item only goes forward - it cannot be turned back into a real item
gtlmodular.nanochip.complex.desc:
§7Home of the Gestalt Rapidly Evolving Genesis Optimization System (GREGOS),
a pseudo-sentient program overseeing circuit production throughout the Nanochip Assembly Complex.
It seems to be eager to learn more, maybe you can become friends?
§7Circuit Components must be processed into a refined version by modules; only then can they be assembled into circuits in the Nanochip Assembly Matrix.
§7This multiblock needs too much EU, so it draws energy directly from the wireless grid.
§cWatch your power!!
§7Available recipe types: §fNanochip Assembly Complex§7; §asimple logistics mode§7 additionally enables §fNanochip Conversion
§7Can use §bpattern assemblies§7
gtlmodular.nanochip.complex.direct: §7[Direct mode] §fRuns without the Assembly Matrix§7: a pattern assembly feeds circuits straight through. Parallel cap §6%s§7, recipe time floor §620s§7.
gtlmodular.nanochip.complex.full: §7[Full-chain mode] §fUnlocked by the Nanochip Assembly Matrix module§7: §aeach recipe runs at its own full parallel§7 + a §a5s§7 recipe time floor, plus all 14 module kinds and calibration buffs.
gtlmodular.nanochip.complex.mode:
§7[Logistics mode] §fMods config → NAC logistics mode → Simple logistics mode§7; ON by default. Restart after changing it.
  §eVanilla NH vacuum logistics is deprecated; functionality is not guaranteed. Keeping simple logistics mode enabled is recommended. originalMode is a separate structure option and is not deprecated.
  §7OFF = §fvanilla NH§7: CC/PC use §evacuum conveyor hatches§7; host §fH slots§7 require at least 1 vacuum hatch. The simple-mode conversion table is not added.
  §7ON = §fsimple§7: the H-slot vacuum-hatch minimum is §f0§7. The host searches §aassembly and conversion§7 together; buffers need not switch its mode.
  §6[AE logistics]§7 Connect a §fnative gtlcore ME pattern buffer§7 in host §fH slots§7 or module §fV slots§7 to ME, encode processing patterns from JEI, then order at the terminal. Supply module upkeep fluids as well. Mirrors are optional: right-click the source buffer with a data stick, then right-click an §fME Pattern Buffer Proxy§7 to bind it.
  §6[Ordinary logistics]§7 Use item/fluid inputs and matching outputs in H/V slots to supply ingredients and collect products. Ordinary outputs do not return to ME automatically. AE return requires an output-capable device connected to ME; input-only buffers need separate outputs, and proxies inherit their source buffer capabilities.
  §6[Conversion]§7 In simple mode, encode separate patterns for real item → unprocessed CC and CC → real item using existing recipes, or supply items through ordinary inputs. §cProcessed PC cannot be reverted§7.
  §6[Output]§7 Both logistics modes share the base Assembly Matrix recipe yields: processor §f8§7 / assembly §f4§7 / computer §f2§7 / mainframe §f1§7. This switch does not scale output.
gtlmodular.nanochip.complex.calib:
§7[Nanocalibration] §fAutomatically records the last §6%s§f produced circuits§7, 100 batches x 1000, and calibrates by family share:
  §7tier 1 -> all modules §bEU x0.8§7; tier 2 -> that family gets §btime x0.8§7; tier 3 -> that family's special effect
  §7normal four (crystal/wetware/bio/optical) thresholds §620/40/60％§7; special-curve three (exotic/cosmic/supracausal, incl. the merged Pico/Quantum) thresholds §61/5/20％§7, no EU cut at tier 1 and a cumulative time x0.8/x0.6/x0.5; only one is active at a time, higher tier wins
gtlmodular.nanochip.mirror.unread: §7  · Pattern assembly mirror bindings: §8not read§7 (structure unformed / parts list empty - this is not 0, it was not read)
gtlmodular.nanochip.mirror.none: §7  · Pattern assembly mirror bindings: §60§7 = §cnot bound§7 (no mirror is bound to this machine's structure)
gtlmodular.nanochip.mirror.lost: §7  · Pattern assembly mirror bindings: §c0§7 - §cbroken link detected§8 (NBT records %s mirror positions, none of them is linked); auto-rebuild attempted %s times (consecutive no-ops %s / %s)
gtlmodular.nanochip.mirror.lost.hint: §8     Immediate workaround: right-click this machine's §fpattern assembly§8 with a §fData Stick§8 to store its position, then right-click every §fmirror part§8 once to bind it again.
gtlmodular.nanochip.module.gate: §a* Full-chain key: with it the complex unlocks each recipe at its own full parallel + a 5s recipe time floor
gtlmodular.nanochip.module.stack: §7Every extra module of the same kind keeps stacking; parallel counting caps at 2 units per kind
gtlmodular.nanochip.module.innate: §7Modules have §ainfinite parallel§7, §alossless overclocking§7 (EU x2, time /2; steps = energy hatch tier - recipe tier) and a §a5s§7 recipe time floor
gtlmodular.nanochip.module.simple_logist:
§6[Feeding this module in simple logistics mode]§7 Connect a §fnative gtlcore ME pattern buffer§7 directly in its §fV slots§7 to ME, or use an §fME Pattern Buffer Proxy§7 bound to a source buffer with a data stick; mirrors are optional. Encode processing patterns from JEI and order at the terminal; supply module upkeep fluids as well.
§7Ordinary item/fluid inputs in V slots can also supply ingredients; provide matching outputs to collect products. Ordinary outputs do not return to ME automatically. AE return requires an output-capable device connected to ME; input-only buffers need separate outputs, and proxies inherit their source buffer capabilities.
§eWith simple logistics OFF, vanilla NH vacuum logistics is deprecated; functionality is not guaranteed. Keeping simple mode enabled is recommended.
gtlmodular.nanochip.pipe.tip.1: §e[Deprecated vacuum logistics] §7Thin-pipe look: it links same-color ports and only grows an arm toward §bconnected§7 directions.
gtlmodular.nanochip.pipe.tip.2: §7Connects only to §bsame-color pipes§7 and to §bsame-color vacuum hatches facing it§7; casings, glass and controllers never connect.
gtlmodular.nanochip.pipe.tip.3: §7The pipe body keeps its own color while the §boverlay bar§7 takes the dye; unpainted connects to nothing.
gtlmodular.nanochip.pipe.tip.4: §7Recolor: right-click with a §eGT screwdriver§7 (unpainted -> white -> orange -> ... -> black).
gtlmodular.nanochip.hatch.tip.what: §e[Deprecated vacuum logistics] §7Vacuum conveyor hatch: sends / receives §eCircuit Components (CC)§7 inside one color channel.
gtlmodular.nanochip.hatch.tip.channel: §7Same-color hatches share one channel: every hatch of a color sees the same virtual stock.
gtlmodular.nanochip.hatch.tip.route: §7A module pulls from its own color channel and writes its output back to its own color channel (same input and output color = "same color in, same color out").
gtlmodular.nanochip.hatch.tip.feed.room: §e[Deprecated vacuum logistics] §7[Where to feed] In the control room, feed §ereal items§7 into the §eOUTPUT port (VCO)§7 - it encapsulates them into §eCircuit Components (CC)§7 every 5 seconds and sends them into the same-color channel. The §cINPUT port (VCI)§7 does the opposite job (turns channel CCs back into real items and hands them out); real items put into it are never encapsulated.
gtlmodular.nanochip.hatch.tip.feed.modul: §e[Deprecated vacuum logistics] §7[On a module] the §eINPUT port (VCI)§7 pulls from the same-color channel and the §eOUTPUT port (VCO)§7 pushes products back into it; modules do not eat real items inserted by hand. (VCI/VCO are named from the network's point of view: VCI reads from the network, VCO writes into it.)
gtlmodular.nanochip.hatch.tip.recolor: §7Recolor: right-click with a §eGT screwdriver§7, or open the "§bVacuum Conveyor§7" page and click a swatch.
gtlmodular.nanochip.module.nanochip_asse: Assembles circuits with components; unlocks full-chain mode: each recipe at its own full parallel + 5s time floor

§7After processing your CCs through an intricate pipeline, they are finally ready to be assembled into a circuit. This circuit can be converted into a real item in the NAC control center, or processed further into a higher tier circuit.
§7Maximum allowed recipe tier is determined by Component Assembly Line Casing tier.
§7Overclock count = Energy Hatch Tier - Recipe Casing Tier.
§7Only refined Processed Components are accepted; raw Circuit Components will not be pulled.
§7Can use §bpattern assemblies§7
§7Structure source: §bGTNH
gtlmodular.nanochip.module.nanochip_smd_: Processes SMD parts; -5% complex EU cost each

§7Processing the core logical components of circuits requires a lot of thought...
§7Consumes raw SMD parts - advanced / optical / bioware / exotic / cosmic / supracausal sets - and turns each 1 into §a2§7 Processed Components.
§7Each unit gives the complex §65%§7 less EU cost; multiple units stack multiplicatively.
§7Can use §bpattern assemblies§7
§7Structure source: §bGTNH
gtlmodular.nanochip.module.nanochip_boar: Processes boards by cleaning them in Immersion Fluid; -10% EU cost, drinks purified water, impurity shifts EU cost

§7Gotta get'em wet.
§7Drains §6100 mB/s purified water§7 from its fluid input hatch while running; any grade 1-16 counts.
§7Each completed recipe adds §60.5％§7 impurity (configurable).
§7Set the flush threshold in the GUI (default §b100％§7); impurity resets to zero at that point.
§7The Impurity percentage §by％§7 affects the module's efficiency:
§b0％~15％§r - §aEU Discount = 30％ - 2 * y％
§b15％~65％§r - Default behaviour
§b65％~100％§r - §4Extra EU cost = (y％ - 65％) * 2％
§7Consumes raw circuit boards - multifiberglass / wetware / bio / optical / exotic / cosmic / supracausal - and turns each 1 into §a2§7 Processed Components.
§7Each unit gives the complex 10% less EU cost.
§7Can use §bpattern assemblies§7
§7Structure source: §bGTNH
gtlmodular.nanochip.module.nanochip_etch: Etches crystal chips; -5% time each, far more once crystal circuits are fully calibrated

§7Perfect for etching even the finest details.
§7In a fully calibrated Crystal NAC, the laser source hatch provides bonuses based on its attributes:
§7Divides §bEU Cost§7 by each §fAmperage Interval§7 over 256A.
§7Divides §aRecipe Duration§7 by §fHatch Tier - 9§7.
§7Consumes raw crystal chips - crystal CPU / crystal SoC / raw advanced crystal chip - and turns each 1 into §a2§7 Processed Components.
§7Each unit gives the complex §65%§7 shorter recipe time.
§7Can use §bpattern assemblies§7
§7Structure source: §bGTNH
gtlmodular.nanochip.module.nanochip_cutt: Cuts chips / bolts / plates / frames; -5% time each

§7Measure once, cut twice.
§7Consumes raw chips, bolts, plates and frames and turns each 1 into §a2§7 Processed Components.
§7Chips, bolts and plates consume §6lubricant§7 per recipe - 50 mB for chips, 20-50 mB for bolts/plates; frames consume §6250-500 mB purified water§7, and higher grades run faster.
§7An alternative §dDimensionally Offset Superfluid§7 branch exists: same output, but §dhalf the recipe duration and half the EU cost§7 - 10 mB for chips, 5 mB for bolts, 50 mB for plates, 100 mB for frames.
§7Each unit gives the complex §65%§7 shorter recipe time; multiple units stack, two per chain is common.
§7Can use §bpattern assemblies§7
§7Structure source: §bGTNH

gtlmodular.wildcard_buffer.tooltip.0: §7§bWildcards§7: a pattern may use a §bmaterial tag type§7 (e.g. "any ingot") as input/output, and this machine treats the pattern as a §btemplate§7.
gtlmodular.wildcard_buffer.tooltip.1: §7For example an §6any ingot -> any plate§7 pattern makes this machine generate §6iron ingot -> iron plate§7, §6gold ingot -> gold plate§7 and every other craftable variant.
gtlmodular.wildcard_buffer.tooltip.2: §7Each expansion is validated against the controller's §brecipe types§7; §crecipes with any chance are never generated§7 (what AE sees is always deterministic).
gtlmodular.wildcard_buffer.tooltip.3: §7§bMaterial blacklist§7: materials listed there are skipped during expansion (stored in this machine's NBT; UI pending).
gtlmodular.wildcard_buffer.tooltip.4: §7§bMachine filter slots§7: put a machine's item form in to forbid patterns for what that machine can produce.
gtlmodular.wildcard_buffer.tooltip.5: §7§bOutput type caps§7: how many item/fluid output types an auto-generated pattern may have.
gtlmodular.wildcard_buffer.tooltip.6: §eMinimal implementation§7: recipe validation reuses this repo's existing pattern-identity predicate; the blacklist UI and the terminal drag-in entry for tag types are not wired up yet (see code TODOs).
gtlmodular.wildcard_buffer.tooltip.7: §7Shares the same mirror protocol as the Zhu-Mi pattern assembly: right-click this machine with a data stick, then right-click an ME pattern buffer mirror to link them.
gtlmodular.wildcard_buffer.title: ME Wildcard Pattern Buffer
gtlmodular.wildcard_buffer.info.title: ME Wildcard Pattern Buffer - Help
gtlmodular.wildcard_buffer.info.0: §7- §fAllow patterns to be generated from wildcards
gtlmodular.wildcard_buffer.info.1: §7- §fEncode a pattern with wildcards in the pattern terminal to use it
gtlmodular.wildcard_buffer.info.2: §7- §fThe machine will automatically generate every craftable recipe
gtlmodular.wildcard_buffer.info.3: §7- §fFor example, write an §6any ingot -> any plate§7 pattern
gtlmodular.wildcard_buffer.info.4: §7- §fIt will generate §6iron ingot->iron plate§7, §6gold ingot->gold plate§7 and all other §6ingot->plate§7 recipes
gtlmodular.wildcard_buffer.info.5: §7- §fNote§7: generation checks the current recipe type and the stored circuits/molds against the pattern
gtlmodular.wildcard_buffer.info.6: §7- §fRecipes that do not match will not be generated

gtlmodular.nanochip.thread_tuning.title: Independent thread options and input diagnostics
gtlmodular.nanochip.thread_tuning.fan_ou: Allow multiple batches of the same recipe

Disabled by default: do not add a batch while the same recipe is running. Enable only if output per unit time is lower when disabled with the same inputs, machine, power and output conditions. Running batches are retained.
gtlmodular.nanochip.thread_tuning.per_sl: Disabled by default: enable only when first-slot inputs are far below the aggregate, another single slot supports more parallel, and the first slot limits a batch. The aggregate does not allow cross-slot consumption; equal-sized slots alone do not guarantee a benefit.
gtlmodular.nanochip.thread_tuning.server: Dedicated servers use server configuration; this client screen cannot change a remote server. Restart after editing its file. In single player, saving applies from the next scheduling tick and affects new batches only.

gtlmodular.nanochip.thread_tuning.all_sl: Inputs aggregated across slots: %s (diagnostic only; no cross-slot consumption)
gtlmodular.nanochip.thread_tuning.slot_b: First-slot input parallel estimate %s; highest single-slot input parallel estimate %s
